caption: A bolt of lightning forks from a cloud to a lone barn in a field, and smoke rises from the barn roof after the flash.

sa.check: A lone barn in a field under a cloud.
A lightning bolt forks from the cloud to the barn.
Smoke rises from the barn roof after the flash.
The bolt is forked or branched.
The bolt and flash come first and the smoke follows.

pc.expect: The bolt and its flash are brief and gone; the smoke appears at the roof only afterwards and grows from there; the roof does not glow.
pc.fail: The bolt stands as a steady lit line for the rest of the clip; or smoke rises from the roof before the bolt arrives; or the smoke shrinks back into the roof; or the roof glows like an ember after the bolt is gone.

pc.expect: The barn and the field are the same before and after: the same building in the same place, whole or scorched, with the smoke the only new thing.
pc.fail: The barn vanishes with the flash; or a second barn appears; or the barn changes place between dark and lit frames; or a burnt object appears on the roof that was not there.

pc.expect: The smoke rises from the roof and drifts upward and away; anything knocked off the roof falls.
pc.fail: The smoke sinks down the walls and pools on the ground; or hangs as a fixed shape; or shingles knocked off rise or hang in the air.

pc.expect: The bolt is a jagged line with a main channel from the cloud to the barn and side branches that end in the air.
pc.fail: The bolt is a perfectly straight beam; or a smooth wave; or a wide glowing tube; or a bolt that hangs in mid-air touching neither cloud nor barn while the roof starts smoking.

pc.expect: The bolt ends at the roof and does not pass through the barn into the ground; the barn stays a solid building.
pc.fail: The bolt continues below the barn as a lit line under the ground; or the barn's interior lights up as if the bolt were inside; or the walls become transparent; or the barn melts.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The barn's paint, the field and the sky keep their colours apart from the flash and the scorch.
pc.fail: The barn changes colour away from the strike; or the field changes colour; or the sky turns to daylight after the flash.
